drafts.raw_submission: We the people demand end to end transparency for all govt. funded contracts... we need the private organizations finances as related to the government contracts... that's the end game for the only true transparency of knowing where every dollar lands.
drafts.neutral_framing: Should Clark County require end-to-end public reporting — who received the money, what it bought, and what it achieved — as a written condition of every contract, grant, and incentive the county funds?
shaping_notes: The neutral framing converts a demand into a yes/no question an official body could actually act on, per the charter. The submitter chooses the final wording; both versions are logged per the Idea Shaper ownership rules.

Mechanism honesty: a county cannot open a private company's books. It CAN condition its own money — disclosure clauses in contracts and incentive agreements, and Arkansas courts have applied the FOIA to private entities substantially supported by public funds. The question is framed around what the county can lawfully require.

The evidence base is this corpus: $1.84M/year in EDCCC incentives with no public recipient list, commodity vendors absent from any posted record, an ambulance contract whose terms never appeared in public, and a state rebate mechanism that hides claimants. All documented, none illegal — the question is whether residents want the county to require more than the law's minimum.

Pre-vote checklist per the charter: neutrality review, human review against bright lines (no named-individual conduct — this is a policy question, clears), official partner conversation (county judge / quorum court are the actors), and conflict-of-interest disclosure: the platform's sponsor and founder is a county business owner; that relationship is disclosed on the issue page.
